data.name: Amariah
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Amariah means 'God is my mountain.' The name Amariah was given to several women in the Bible. In the Old Testament, Amariah is the name of a priest who brings a message from the Lord to King Hezekiah. In the New Testament, Amariah is mentioned as one of the holy women who anointed Jesus' feet with expensive perfume.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of God's protection and strength.
data.numerology_meaning: A name of creativity, self-expression, and communication.

data.cultural_impact: The name Amariah, derived from the Hebrew language, has been used significantly in the cultural contexts of Judaism and Christianity. In Judaism, the name Amariah is mentioned in the midrashic literature as the name of a Levite who was one of the teachers of King Josiah. In Christianity, Amariah is a name that resonates with devotion and devotion to God. The name carries a sense of strong faith and steadfastness, reflecting the strength and resilience of those who have endured in their faith.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Amariah holds great spiritual significance for those who bear it, as it is a reminder of the powerful presence of God in our lives. The name carries the message that God is our solid foundation, our unyielding rock, and our unwavering strength. It encourages us to trust in the Lord, to lean on Him in times of need, and to find our security and refuge in Him. The name inspires us to live our lives in a way that reflects our faith and devotion to God, striving to live in accordance with His will and to bring glory to His name.

historical_references.reference: Amariah, the wife of Joram, is mentioned in 2 Kings 14:21. She is said to have given birth to a son named Azariah, also known as Uzziah.
historical_references.context: The Bible reference is from the Old Testament, specifically the books of Kings. Amariah was the wife of King Joram of Judah and birthed a son named Azariah who later became a respected King of Judah under the name Uzziah.

historical_references.reference: Amariah, the wife of Josiah, is mentioned in the apocryphal text 'The Second Book of the Maccabees'. She is said to have helped her husband in the fight against the Syrians during the Maccabean revolt in the late 2nd century BC.
historical_references.context: The Apocrypha are texts that were not included in the original Hebrew Bible but were added to the Greek Septuagint. Amariah, daughter of Jason, was the wife of King Josiah of Judah and played an active role in the Maccabean revolt. She helped her husband in the fight against the Syrians and is remembered for her courage and support during this time of conflict.

It is a Hebrew name meaning 'exalted God' and has a rich biblical background. Amariah can be found on various contemporary Christian music platforms such as YouTube Music, Spotify, and Apple Music. The name also fits into current trends towards unique and meaningful names, as well as a return to traditional biblical names.
